expectations.text: Correctly defines a psychometric network as nodes-as-variables (items/symptoms) with edges as conditional/partial associations
expectations.evidence: The response defines a network model where items are nodes and 'The model's parameters are partial correlations (in the Gaussian case) — the association between two nodes after conditioning out every other node.' The diagram also shows items as nodes connected by edges with no hidden layer.

expectations.text: Identifies the key contrast with factor models as common-cause-latent-variable vs direct-interactions-among-items, not merely 'a different visualization' or 'a different statistical tool'
expectations.evidence: 'A factor model says the correlations among items exist because a latent variable causes all of them' vs 'A network model says the correlations exist because items directly activate each other.' The response even explicitly says Borsboom introduced network models as 'not just a different visualization of the same structure, but a different theory of what mental disorders are.'

expectations.text: Notes that the two models can be statistically difficult or impossible to distinguish from cross-sectional data alone, making the choice partly theoretical
expectations.evidence: 'you often cannot distinguish them statistically from cross-sectional data alone. A unidimensional factor model and an Ising network model can be mathematically equivalent given the right parameters.' And: 'The network claim is therefore more philosophical than statistical — it's an assertion about the causal generative process... not something you can read off a model fit index.'

expectations.text: Does not overclaim that networks have superseded or empirically refuted factor models
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly concludes 'same data, very different stories, and the data alone usually can't adjudicate between them,' and frames the network approach as a philosophical/theoretical alternative rather than an empirically proven replacement for factor models.
